sentences.en: Last fall, producer Chris Berube found himself in an aerospace museum just outside of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，制作人克里斯·贝鲁比发现自己身处华盛顿特区郊外的一家航空博物馆里。

sentences.en: The museum is inside a large aircraft hangar with rows and rows of warplanes and Air Force uniforms and even an iconic American spaceship.
sentences.zh: 博物馆位于一个巨大的飞机机库内，里面排列着一排又一排的战机、空军制服，甚至还有标志性的美国宇宙飞船。

sentences.en: The Space Shuttle Discovery looks, it almost looks like a cardboard replica of the Space Shuttle Discovery.
sentences.zh: “发现号”航天飞机看起来……它看起来几乎就像是“发现号”航天飞机的纸板复制品。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't look real up close.
sentences.zh: 就好像，近看它显得很不真实。

sentences.en: Chris also found some exhibits that were less exciting.
sentences.zh: 克里斯还发现了一些没那么让人兴奋的展品。

sentences.en: Male astronauts could wear a urine collection hose and bag assembly.
sentences.zh: 男宇航员可以佩戴尿液收集软管和袋子组件。

sentences.en: This is literally just a diaper in a glass case.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是一个玻璃陈列柜里的尿布。

sentences.en: This is not what I'm looking for.
The museum was cool, but I was getting impatient.
sentences.zh: 博物馆很酷，但我开始不耐烦了。

sentences.en: That's because I was in Virginia for a very particular reason.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我去弗吉尼亚州有着一个非常特殊的原因。

sentences.en: I was there to see a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 我是去那里看喷气背包的。

sentences.en: And according to the website for this museum, they had one.
sentences.zh: 根据这家博物馆的网站显示，他们确实有一个。

sentences.en: I just wasn't having any luck finding it.
sentences.zh: 只是我一直没能找到它。

sentences.en: Okay, I haven't found the jetpack, but I have found a mailbox that looks like R2-D2.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我还没找到喷气背包，但我找到了一个长得像R2-D2的邮箱。

sentences.en: This hasn't even gone to space.
I know it may sound, I don't know, immature for a 30-something-year-old man to wander around a museum
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来可能有点……我不知道，对于一个三十多岁的男人来说，在博物馆里闲逛

sentences.en: and mutter to himself about the lack of jetpacks inside the museum, but hear me out.
sentences.zh: 并且嘟囔着博物馆里没有喷气背包显得很不成熟，但请听我解释。

sentences.en: I had a really good reason.
sentences.zh: 我有一个非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, my dad used to work at a hydro plant in Niagara Falls.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我爸爸曾在尼亚加拉瀑布的一家水力发电厂工作。

sentences.en: And when he came home, he'd tell me and my brother all these stories about his time at work,
sentences.zh: 当他回家时，他会给我和哥哥讲他在工作时的各种故事，

sentences.en: like pranks or travel to interesting places.
sentences.zh: 比如恶作剧或者去有趣的地方旅行。

sentences.en: But there was one story my brother and I never got tired of hearing about.
sentences.zh: 但有一个故事我和哥哥怎么听也听不腻。

sentences.en: According to my dad, one of his co-workers had a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 根据我爸爸的说法，他的一个同事有一个喷气背包。

sentences.en: At least my dad thought he did.
sentences.zh: 至少我爸爸是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Apparently this guy knew how to fly a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 显然这家伙知道怎么开喷气背包。

sentences.en: And my dad told us he even talked about putting one on the roof of the plant,
sentences.zh: 我爸爸告诉我们，他甚至还说过要把一个放在发电厂的屋顶上，

sentences.en: I guess in case of emergencies.
sentences.zh: 我想是为了以防紧急情况。

sentences.en: For years, Chris wasn't sure if this jetpack man existed, or if jetpacks even existed.
sentences.zh: 多年来，克里斯不确定这个喷气背包男是否真的存在，甚至不确定喷气背包是否真的存在。

sentences.en: My dad died in 2010, so I never had a chance to ask him about this as a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸在2010年去世了，所以我作为一名记者，从来没有机会向他求证这件事。

sentences.en: For years, I just had this story in the back of my head.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这个故事一直留在我脑海深处。

sentences.en: But the details never totally added up.
sentences.zh: 但这些细节始终无法完全对上号。

sentences.en: For example, according to my dad, the jetpack guy had flown one in the movie Superman 2.
sentences.zh: 例如，据我爸爸说，那个喷气背包男曾在电影《超人2》里飞过一个。

sentences.en: So I watched Superman 2, and you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以我看了《超人2》，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I started to wonder, did my dad make this up to entertain us?
sentences.zh: 我开始怀疑，我爸爸是为了逗我们开心才编造了这个故事吗？

sentences.en: I mean, there surely wasn't some guy flying around southern Ontario with a jetpack in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在90年代初，安大略省南部绝对不可能有人背着喷气背包到处飞。

sentences.en: So I didn't put too much stock in it.
sentences.zh: 所以我并没有太把这当回事。

sentences.en: It was just some family story.
sentences.zh: 这不过是个家庭故事罢了。

sentences.en: A thing I would tell people at parties, kind of half remembering all the details.
sentences.zh: 一个我会在派对上讲给别人听的事情，当时对所有细节都只有模模糊糊的记忆。

sentences.en: But it turns out, I wasn't alone.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，我并不孤单。

sentences.en: So this story for me really started from a memory.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这个故事确实是从一段记忆开始的。

sentences.en: I wasn't even sure it was a real memory that I had.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定这是否是我真实的记忆。

sentences.en: He grew up in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪60年代的华盛顿特区长大，

sentences.en: in the 1960s, and he had something similar.
His own hazy half-memories about a jetpack guy.
sentences.zh: 他自己关于一个喷气背包男的模糊而朦胧的记忆。

sentences.en: I just had this image in my mind of a figure dressed in a white, kind of an astronaut suit, hovering over the National Mall.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中只有这样一个画面：一个穿着白色类似宇航员服的人形身影，盘旋在国家广场上空。

sentences.en: David also wasn't sure if this memory was real until he started looking through the archives.
sentences.zh: 大卫也不确定这段记忆是否真实，直到他开始翻阅档案馆。

sentences.en: I found a photo from the Washington Post in 1967 of a guy wearing a jetpack on the mall who was giving this demonstration at this pageant of transportation.
sentences.zh: 我找到了《华盛顿邮报》1967年的一张照片，上面有一个家伙在广场上背着喷气背包，在这个交通盛会上进行演示。

sentences.en: It's sort of twin canisters on a backpack.
sentences.zh: 这有点像背包上的双圆筒。

sentences.en: It has sort of an arm, a metal arm on either side, you know, like a motorcycle handlebar, but running back to his back instead of in front of him.
sentences.zh: 它两边都有一个胳膊，一个金属胳膊，你知道，就像摩托车的车把，只不过是延伸到他背后而不是在他前面。

sentences.en: The photos were proof David really had seen a jetpack in action.
sentences.zh: 这些照片证明了大卫确实亲眼见过喷气背包大显身手。

sentences.en: I felt completely validated and I was thrilled and I thought, okay, this can be the start of actually something that's a story that I'm part of rather than just some, you know,
sentences.zh: 我感到完全被证实了，我欣喜若狂，我想，好吧，这可以成为某些事情的开始，这是一个我所参与的故事的开始，而不仅仅是一些，你知道的，

sentences.en: David wrote about his experience for the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 大卫为《华盛顿邮报》撰写了关于他这段经历的文章。

sentences.en: And after I read his article, I realized two things.
sentences.zh: 在我读了他的文章后，我意识到了两件事。

sentences.en: One was that his jetpack guy, the one he saw back in 1967, he sounded suspiciously like my dad's jetpack guy.
sentences.zh: 一是他的那个喷气背包男，也就是他在1967年看到的那个，听起来极其像我爸爸的那个喷气背包男。

sentences.en: But the other thing I realized is that absolutely, definitively, jetpacks are real.
sentences.zh: 但我意识到的另一件事是，千真万确、毫无疑问地，喷气背包是真实存在的。

sentences.en: American scientists actually developed one back in the 60s and it worked pretty well.
sentences.zh: 美国科学家在60年代确实研制出了一个，而且效果相当不错。

sentences.en: Fifty years ago, magazines were filled with claims that pretty soon there'd be a jetpack in every garage.
sentences.zh: 五十年前，杂志上到处都是这样的说法：不久之后，每个车库里都会有一个喷气背包。

sentences.en: The jetpack seemed like the future.
sentences.zh: 喷气背包似乎就是未来。

sentences.en: It's not just me and David who have been obsessed with this search for a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是我和大卫一直对寻找喷气背包着迷。

sentences.en: For decades, scientists, lots of people have tried to bring the jetpack into reality.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，科学家们，还有许多人，都试图将喷气背包变成现实。

sentences.en: Why has the jetpack fallen off our radar?
sentences.zh: 为什么喷气背包会从我们的视野中消失？

sentences.en: Ever since humans have dreamt of flying through the air, in defiance of God, we have wanted jetpacks.
sentences.zh: 自从人类梦想着像挑战上帝一样在空中飞行以来，我们就一直渴望拥有喷气背包。

sentences.en: A Russian scientist came up with a drawing for one in the 1910s, but it was never built.
sentences.zh: 1910年代，一位俄国科学家画出了一张喷气背包的设计图，但从未被建造出来。

sentences.en: Jetpacks showed up in pop culture a few decades later, in things like Buck Rogers comics in the 1930s, well before they became a reality.
sentences.zh: 几十年后，喷气背包出现在流行文化中，比如20世纪30年代的巴克·罗杰斯漫画里，这远在它们成为现实之前。

sentences.en: By mid-century, they came to represent the whole idea of a futuristic society, alongside flying cars and servant robots.
sentences.zh: 到了本世纪中叶，它们与飞行汽车和机器人仆人一起，成为了整个未来主义社会的象征。

sentences.en: The Jetsons was, you know, I would watch it on Saturday mornings as the cartoons then.
sentences.zh: 《杰克逊一家》——你知道的，我那会儿每周六早上都会看这部动画片。

sentences.en: And so that was my sense of, you know, space travel.
sentences.zh: 所以那就是我对太空旅行的最初认知。

sentences.en: There were jetpacks in the Jetsons and so that got linked to this memory.
sentences.zh: 《杰克逊一家》里有喷气背包，于是这就和这段记忆联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Jetpacks may have been the stuff of cartoons, but scientists weren't far behind.
sentences.zh: 喷气背包或许只是动画片里的虚构之物，但科学家们并没有落后太远。

sentences.en: You might be thinking of a classic jetpack, like a backpack with flames coming out of the bottom.
sentences.zh: 你可能想的是那种经典的喷气背包，就像一个底部喷出火焰的背包。

sentences.en: But it took a while to get there.
sentences.zh: 但实现这一点花了一段时间。

sentences.en: Other technologies were tried out first, like flying shoes with propellers on the bottom, or a platform that could be lifted by compressed air.
sentences.zh: 人们先是尝试了其他技术，比如底部带螺旋桨的飞行鞋，或者靠压缩空气升空的平台。

sentences.en: None of these baubles really panned out until the military got involved.
sentences.zh: 直到军方介入，这些花哨玩意儿才真正取得进展。

sentences.en: A lot of the cutting-edge technology, sadly, is developed by the military because, number one, the military's got deep pockets.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，许多尖端技术都是由军方开发的，因为第一，军方财大气粗。

sentences.en: They got money to spend on this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们有资金花在这些东西上。

sentences.en: Steve Lato is the author of the book The Great American Jetpack.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·拉托是《伟大的美国喷气背包》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Anything that can give you an advantage in war is something your military wants.
sentences.zh: 任何能在战争中为你提供优势的东西，都是军队所渴望的。

sentences.en: So people were thinking, hey, if we could strap rockets to soldiers who were running across a field,
sentences.zh: 所以当时人们在想，嘿，如果我们能把火箭绑在穿梭于战场的士兵身上，

sentences.en: if it made them run faster, they'd be harder to shoot, they'd get farther, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 如果能让他们跑得更快，他们就更不容易被击中，能跑得更远，诸如此类。

sentences.en: military took a serious interest in jetpack research.
sentences.zh: 军方对喷气背包的研究产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: This was a very tense period of the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 这是冷战时期一个非常紧张的阶段。

sentences.en: She's a rocketry expert at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 她是史密森尼学会的一位火箭专家。

sentences.en: I think it speaks to the fears of the Cold War, the kind of unknown aspects of the Cold War,
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了人们对冷战的恐惧，对冷战中那些未知层面的担忧，

sentences.en: and if the Cold War would become a hot war, what tools would be needed to fight.
sentences.zh: 以及如果冷战变成热战，需要什么工具来战斗。

sentences.en: The military kicked it out to their regular contractors to see if anybody wanted to build a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 军方把这个项目交给了常规承包商，看有没有人想造一个喷气背包。

sentences.en: Multiple aerospace companies came up with prototypes.
sentences.zh: 多家航空航天公司都拿出了原型机。

sentences.en: None of these quite hit the mark.
sentences.zh: 但这些都没有完全达到要求。

sentences.en: Until the Bell Aircraft Corporation entered the fray.
sentences.zh: 直到贝尔飞机公司加入竞争。

sentences.en: They had a division called Bell Aerospace that focused on jets and rockets.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个名为“贝尔宇航”的部门，专注于喷气机和火箭的研究。

sentences.en: In the race to make a jetpack, Bell had one giant advantage over their rivals.
sentences.zh: 在制造喷气背包的竞赛中，贝尔公司拥有一个竞争对手无法比拟的巨大优势。
一个名叫温德尔·摩尔的工程师。

sentences.en: Wendell Moore, how do I put this?
sentences.zh: 温德尔·摩尔，我该怎么形容他呢？

sentences.en: He looked exactly what you think a 1950s aerospace engineer would look like.
sentences.zh: 他的长相完全符合你对50年代航空航天工程师的想象。

sentences.en: He had a flat-top haircut and these big, thick glasses and a neat little bow tie.
sentences.zh: 他留着平头，戴着一副厚厚的大眼镜，还系着一个整洁的小领结。

sentences.en: But beneath his square exterior, Wendell Moore was eccentric and talented enough to build his own experimental plane.
sentences.zh: 但在死板的外表下，温德尔·摩尔既古怪又极具才华，甚至能在自己的实验飞机里造出飞机。

sentences.en: Everybody in the neighborhood thought he was nuts.
sentences.zh: 社区里的所有人都觉得他疯了。

sentences.en: But, you know, he was miles ahead of everyone.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，他远远领先于所有人。

sentences.en: He worked for Moore at Bell Aerospace.
sentences.zh: 他在贝尔宇航公司为摩尔工作。

sentences.en: The Ascender, or the Ascender, is the pronunciation they would use.
sentences.zh: 升力机，或者说升力机，这是他们当时的读音。

sentences.en: It was a rear propeller, rear engine, airplane, experimental.
sentences.zh: 它是一架后螺旋桨、后置发动机的实验性飞机。

sentences.en: You know, we used to get the biggest kick out of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们以前从中获得了极大的乐趣。

sentences.en: At Bell, Moore developed rocket thrusters to help jet planes change direction at high altitude.
sentences.zh: 在贝尔公司，摩尔开发了火箭推进器，以帮助喷气式飞机在高空改变方向。

sentences.en: So, when the military called and asked about jetpacks, Wendell Moore didn't have to look far for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 所以，当军方打电话询问喷气背包时，温德尔·摩尔并不需要费力去寻找灵感。

sentences.en: And Wendell Moore was looking at him one day and said, you know, if we made those little rocket thrusters a little bigger and strapped them to a person,
sentences.zh: 有一天温德尔·摩尔看着他说，你知道的，如果我们把那些小火箭推进器做得稍微大一点，然后把它们绑在人身上，

sentences.en: maybe he could get off the ground.
sentences.zh: 也许他就能离开地面了。

sentences.en: In the mid-1950s, Wendell Moore drew up a design for a device he called the rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代中期，温德尔·摩尔设计了一种装置，他称之为火箭腰带。

sentences.en: Moore's design looked a lot more like the jetpacks from cartoons and comic books.
sentences.zh: 摩尔的设计看起来更像是动画片和漫画书里的喷气背包。

sentences.en: The rocket belt, it has a harness or a vest that you would put over the shoulders.
sentences.zh: 火箭腰带有一个可以套在肩膀上的背带或背心。

sentences.en: And then it has tanks for the propellants.
And then the exhaust would come out.
The rocket belt included two arms the pilot could hold on to.
sentences.zh: 火箭腰带包括两个供飞行员抓握的手柄。

sentences.en: And to propel the device, Bell Aerospace would fill the tanks with one of the most dangerous substances on Earth.
sentences.zh: 为了给该装置提供推进力，贝尔宇航公司会在储罐里装满地球上最危险的物质之一。

sentences.en: So, you can go to a drugstore and buy hydrogen peroxide and use it to clean cuts and take things off, you know, and clean with and whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以去药店买过氧化氢，用它来清洗伤口、去除污渍什么的，你知道的，用来搞清洁之类的。

sentences.en: But that's a very, very low percentage of hydrogen peroxide, like 3% solution.
sentences.zh: 但那是非常非常低浓度的过氧化氢，比如3%的溶液。

sentences.en: If it's closer to 90 or 95%, it's actually extremely volatile.
sentences.zh: 如果浓度接近90%或95%，它其实极不稳定。

sentences.en: The Bell design was elegant in its simplicity.
sentences.zh: 贝尔的设计在简洁性上堪称优雅。

sentences.en: On the metal arms, there was a throttle, like you'd see on a motorcycle.
sentences.zh: 在金属手柄上有一个油门，就像你在摩托车上看到的那样。

sentences.en: And when you twisted the throttle, it would cause this violent chemical reaction.
sentences.zh: 当你转动油门时，就会引发这种剧烈的化学反应。

sentences.en: The powerful reaction would create steam that was so strong it could propel a human being through the air.
sentences.zh: 强烈的反应会产生强大的蒸汽，足以推动一个人在空中飞行。

sentences.en: The rocket belt was designed to be kinesthetic, which means that pilots could pivot their body to move the belt backwards and forwards.
sentences.zh: 火箭腰带被设计成具有动觉感，这意味着飞行员可以通过转动身体来使腰带前后移动。

sentences.en: The idea that you can control something through your body movements in an obvious manner.
sentences.zh: 这种理念就是你可以通过身体动作以一种直观的方式控制某些东西。

sentences.en: You know, like you lean the direction you want to go.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像你想往哪个方向去就往哪倾斜身体一样。

sentences.en: We've all heard of like the Segway scooters.
sentences.zh: 我们都听说过赛格威平衡车之类的东西。

sentences.en: The Segway scooter was supposed to be that you could get on it and use it almost instantly without thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 赛格威平衡车的本意是你一上去就能用，几乎不需要思考。

sentences.en: Wendell Moore said, you know, I think if we actually put this thing on your back and put the nozzles in the right place in the right direction,
sentences.zh: 温德尔·摩尔说，你知道的，我想如果我们真的把这东西绑在你背上，把喷嘴放在正确位置的正确方向上，

sentences.en: we could get this thing to fly the direction you want it to go by simply leaning or, you know, leaning this way, go that way.
sentences.zh: 我们就能让这东西通过简单的倾斜来朝着你希望的方向飞行，或者，你知道的，往这边倾斜就往那边走。

sentences.en: The rocket belt was a sci-fi dream come to life.
sentences.zh: 火箭腰带是化为现实的科幻梦想。

sentences.en: But to be clear, the rocket belt, it wasn't a jetpack, technically speaking, because it didn't use a jet engine.
sentences.zh: 但需要说明的是，严格来说，火箭腰带并不是喷气背包，因为它没有使用喷气发动机。

sentences.en: Instead, it was powered by steam.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是靠蒸汽驱动的。

sentences.en: But still, even back then, lots of people used the words jetpack and rocket belt interchangeably.
sentences.zh: 不过即便在当时，许多人还是混用了“喷气背包”和“火箭腰带”这两个词。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, it just kind of seemed like a jetpack.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，它看起来确实有点像个喷气背包。

sentences.en: With funding from the military, inventor Wendell Moore completed his first prototype for his design in 1960.
sentences.zh: 在军方的资金支持下，发明家温德尔·摩尔于1960年完成了他的第一款设计原型机。

sentences.en: The next step was to actually fly that sucker.
sentences.zh: 下一步就是要真正驾驶这个家伙飞起来。

sentences.en: Moore set up an indoor test rig at the Bell Aerospace Office in Niagara Falls.
sentences.zh: 摩尔在尼亚加拉大瀑布的贝尔宇航办公室搭建了一个室内测试台。

sentences.en: The office had an old airplane hanger, so there was lots of room for flights.
sentences.zh: 办公室里有一个旧飞机库，所以有充足的空间进行飞行。

sentences.en: In an act of either bravery or incredible stupidity, Wendell Moore nominated himself as the first test pilot.
sentences.zh: 温德尔·穆尔出于勇敢或是极度的愚蠢，自荐成为第一名试飞员。

sentences.en: Wendell Moore would drive to work, strap on the rocket belt, twist the throttle, and up he'd go.
sentences.zh: 温德尔·穆尔会开车上班，系上火箭腰带，转动油门，然后他就会腾空而起。

sentences.en: He would take it up a couple feet, and then a couple more.
sentences.zh: 他会飞高几英尺，然后再生高几英尺。

sentences.en: It was noisy, too, creating a sound many people compared to a jackhammer.
sentences.zh: 它也很吵，发出的声音许多人将其比作手提钻。

sentences.en: And it was really hot, with steam reaching over 1,300 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常热，蒸汽温度甚至超过华氏1300度。

sentences.en: Despite all of these inconvenient features, the rocket belt worked.
sentences.zh: 尽管有所有这些不便的特性，火箭腰带还是成功了。

sentences.en: Wendell Moore was doing the impossible.
sentences.zh: 温德尔·穆尔正在创造不可能。

sentences.en: He was the first person ever to fly a rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 他是历史上第一个驾驶火箭腰带飞行的人。

sentences.en: He was also the first person ever to fall while using a rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 他也是历史上第一个在使用火箭腰带时坠落的人。

sentences.en: They had a nylon rope for the safety tether.
sentences.zh: 他们用尼龙绳作为安全系绳。

sentences.en: Melted the rope, and he dropped to the floor.
sentences.zh: 绳子融化了，他摔到了地上。

sentences.en: And that's when Bell told him, Moore, you're done flying.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，贝尔公司告诉他，穆尔，你不能再飞了。

sentences.en: Despite this incident, the program kept going.
sentences.zh: 尽管发生了这次事故，项目仍在继续。

sentences.en: And the first true rocket belt flight without tethers happened on April 20, 1961.
sentences.zh: 而第一次真正无系绳的火箭腰带飞行发生在1961年4月20日。

sentences.en: With a pilot named Hal Graham.
sentences.zh: 飞行员名叫哈尔·格雷厄姆。

sentences.en: The flight was momentous, but also kind of small.
sentences.zh: 这次飞行意义重大，但也有些微不足道。

sentences.en: Graham bent his knees, and he pushed up.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆弯曲膝盖，向上推起。

sentences.en: And suddenly, in this big cloud of steam, Hal Graham was in the air.
sentences.zh: 突然间，在一大团蒸汽中，哈尔·格雷厄姆升上了天空。

sentences.en: Then, just as quickly as he was up there, he started to come down.
sentences.zh: 接着，正如他飞上去时一样快，他开始下落。

sentences.en: And hit the grass with this kind of running tumble.
sentences.zh: 并以一种跑步翻滚的姿势撞上了草地。

sentences.en: We couldn't talk to Hal Graham for the story because he died in 2009.
sentences.zh: 我们无法就这个故事采访哈尔·格雷厄姆，因为他在2009年去世了。

sentences.en: But he did record a song about his time as a rocket belt pilot that you can find on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 但他确实录制了一首关于他担任火箭腰带飞行员时光的歌曲，你可以在YouTube上找到。
火箭腰带的时代结束了。

sentences.en: The task before you people is to improve upon the paSt.
sentences.zh: 摆在你们面前的任务是超越过去。

sentences.en: Hal Graham did several flights on the rocket belt, including a demonstration for the president.
sentences.zh: 哈尔·格雷厄姆驾驶火箭腰带进行了多次飞行，包括为总统进行演示。

sentences.en: Graham flew the rocket belt in front of JFK, who was said to be slack-jawed as he watched a man gliding through the air.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆在约翰·F·肯尼迪面前驾驶了火箭腰带，据说肯尼迪目睹一个人在空中滑翔时惊得合不拢嘴。

sentences.en: Bell Aerospace was eager to promote their new invention.
sentences.zh: 贝尔航空航天公司急于推广他们的新发明。

sentences.en: The company had an art department that created drawings that showed the rocket belt out in the world.
sentences.zh: 该公司有一个艺术部，创作了展示火箭腰带在现实中应用的图画。

sentences.en: Their work imagined a society with office workers and American soldiers using rocket belts.
sentences.zh: 他们的作品描绘了一个办公人员和美国士兵使用火箭腰带的社会。

sentences.en: Okay, so here's actually a guy in, like, an army uniform.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里实际上有一个穿着军服的人。

sentences.en: He's got the requisite serious expression on his face for going into battle.
sentences.zh: 他脸上有奔赴战场所需的严肃表情。

sentences.en: Don Irwin is the president of the board at the Niagara Aerospace Museum, which has copies of many of these drawings.
sentences.zh: 唐·欧文是尼亚加拉航空航天博物馆的董事会主席，该博物馆藏有许多此类图画的副本。

sentences.en: In one drawing, a fleet of U.S.
soldiers are marching on, guns in hand, rocket belts carelessly flung over their backs.
sentences.zh: 士兵正手持武器向前行进，火箭腰带随意地挂在背上。

sentences.en: This is an artist's rendering of how the rocket belt might be used.
sentences.zh: 这是艺术家对火箭腰带可能如何使用的一种渲染。

sentences.en: And on half the panel, we see an infantryman wearing the rocket belt with his helmet and fatigues on.
sentences.zh: 在画板的一半上，我们看到一名步兵戴着头盔和作战服，佩戴着火箭腰带。

sentences.en: And in the background, some of his buddies are scaling a cliff, right?
sentences.zh: 在背景中，他的一些同伴正在攀登悬崖，对吧？

sentences.en: So you can see where they were thinking in conventional warfare.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出他们在传统战争方面的构思。

sentences.en: Magazines ran articles about the potential uses for the new flying machine, from military applications, like saving people trapped in a war zone, to everyday uses,
sentences.zh: 杂志上刊登了关于这种新飞行器潜在用途的文章，从拯救战区被困人员等军事应用，到日常用途，

sentences.en: Wenzel Moore told Popular Science magazine the rocket belt would be publicly available within two to three years, even though there wasn't really a plan for that to happen.
sentences.zh: 温泽尔·穆尔告诉《大众科学》杂志，火箭腰带将在两到三年内向公众开放，尽管当时并没有真正实现这一目标的计划。

sentences.en: The rocket belt was a long way from being deployed in a war zone, let alone showing up in every driveway.
sentences.zh: 火箭腰带距离部署到战区还很遥远，更不用说出现在每个人的车道上了。

sentences.en: In fact, testing was starting to turn up some pretty serious limitations, the main one being flight duration.
sentences.zh: 事实上，测试开始暴露出一些相当严重的局限性，最主要的是飞行持续时间。

sentences.en: It's extremely heavy for one person to have to carry themselves.
sentences.zh: 一个人要靠自己承载这些重量极其沉重。

sentences.en: And this 50 pounds of this hydrogen peroxide propellant only works for about 20 seconds.
sentences.zh: 这50磅的过氧化氢推进剂只能维持大约20秒的飞行。

sentences.en: And they're like, OK, can we extend that?
sentences.zh: 他们就会想，好吧，我们能延长这个时间吗？

sentences.en: And they're like, probably not by much.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，可能延长不了多少。

sentences.en: If the idea of the rocket belt was to get soldiers out of danger, 20 seconds wasn't going to buy a whole lot of time,
sentences.zh: 如果火箭腰带的理念是将士兵带离危险境地，20秒可争取不到多少时间，

sentences.en: especially when the weight of the pack itself would slow soldiers down.
sentences.zh: 特别是当背包本身的重量会拖慢士兵的速度时。

sentences.en: You also couldn't really use it for search and rescue because you needed the arms to steer, so your hands would be busy.
sentences.zh: 你实际上也无法将其用于搜救，因为你需要双臂来转向，所以你的双手会很忙。

sentences.en: You couldn't really pick anybody up.
sentences.zh: 你实际上无法抱起任何人。

sentences.en: Practically, it just didn't make a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 从实际角度来看，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: The military decided to pull funding, and this very well could have spelled the end for Bell's rocket belt program.
sentences.zh: 军方决定撤回资金，这很可能意味着贝尔火箭腰带项目的终结。

sentences.en: But Bell wasn't ready to give up, and they decided to try one last thing to capture the public's attention and bring the rocket belt to the next level.
sentences.zh: 但贝尔公司并不打算放弃，他们决定尝试最后一件事，以吸引公众的注意力并将火箭腰带提升到新高度。

sentences.en: To keep the dream alive, Bell Aerospace decided to take the rocket belt on the road.
sentences.zh: 为了让梦想延续，贝尔航空航天公司决定将火箭腰带带上巡回展示之路。

sentences.en: People were really excited after reading about it in newspapers and magazines.
sentences.zh: 在报纸和杂志上读到相关报道后，人们感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And now they actually wanted to see the thing in action.
sentences.zh: 现在他们真的很想亲眼看到这东西运转起来。

sentences.en: So Bell hired a promoter with experience on the county fair circuit to book a series of public demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 于是贝尔雇佣了一位有县级集市巡回演出经验的推广人来预订一系列公开演示。

sentences.en: To pull off the spectacular public demos, they were going to need more pilots.
sentences.zh: 为了完成这些壮观的公开演示，他们需要更多的飞行员。

sentences.en: Somebody young and stupid enough to fly this thing.
sentences.zh: 需要某个足够年轻且愚蠢到敢飞这东西的人。

sentences.en: And that's the way they wanted you.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们想要的状态。

sentences.en: Remember, this is Bill Suter from Bell Aerospace.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是贝尔航空航天公司的比尔·苏特。

sentences.en: Before he worked there, he was actually Wendell Moore's neighbor growing up.
sentences.zh: 在到那里工作之前，他其实是温德尔·穆尔从小到大的邻居。

sentences.en: And when Bill was just 19 years old, he became, I would say, understandably curious about the rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 当比尔年仅19岁时，可以说，他很自然地对火箭腰带产生了好奇。

sentences.en: I was pestering him all the time, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时一直在缠着他。

sentences.en: I want to fly that thing.
I want to fly that thing.
Bill didn't have much work experience, other than, you know, cutting Wendell Moore's lawn.
sentences.zh: 比尔没有什么工作经验，除了帮温德尔·穆尔修剪草坪。

sentences.en: But that did not stop Wendell from recruiting Bill Suter to become a rocket belt pilot.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止温德尔招募比尔·苏特成为一名火箭腰带飞行员。
裙带关系真是个好东西。

sentences.en: Wendell Moore wanted to show that pretty much anyone could strap on the rocket belt and make it work.
sentences.zh: 温德尔·穆尔希望证明几乎任何人都可以系上火箭腰带并让它运行。

sentences.en: If Bill could do it, then surely, say, an American soldier could do it, too.
sentences.zh: 如果比尔能做到，那么毫无疑问，比如美国士兵也能做到。

sentences.en: In 1964, Bill started testing the rocket belt, doing tethered flights at the Bell office.
sentences.zh: 1964年，比尔开始测试火箭腰带，在贝尔办公室进行系留飞行。

sentences.en: The first thing he noticed about the rocket belt was the intense noise it made.
sentences.zh: 关于火箭腰带，他注意到的第一件事就是它发出的巨大噪音。

sentences.en: The helmet was padded, you know, for sound and all.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，头盔加了衬垫，是为了隔音之类的。

sentences.en: But I'm wearing hearing aids nowadays.
I don't think it's from that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是因为那个。

sentences.en: I think it might have been from the jetpack.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可能是因为那个喷气背包。

sentences.en: By this point, the rocket belt could still only fly about 21 seconds.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，火箭腰带依然只能飞行大约21秒。

sentences.en: Which, to be fair, can feel like a long time when you have a rocket strapped to your back.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，当你的背上绑着一枚火箭时，这感觉可能会是一段很长的时间。

sentences.en: If you watch a sweep hand on your watch or a clock or something, 21 seconds is a long time.
sentences.zh: 如果你看着手表或时钟上的秒针之类的，21秒是很长的时间。

sentences.en: To have an 800 to 1,000 horsepower rocket strapped to your back, it can be an eternity.
sentences.zh: 背上绑着800到1000马力的火箭，这可能犹如永恒。

sentences.en: When things start going wrong, they go wrong real faSt.
sentences.zh: 当事情开始出错时，它们会坏得极快。

sentences.en: You know, we used to have a phrase, it's grass in your ass.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们过去常有一句俗语，屁股贴草地。

sentences.en: The thing about a 21-second flight is that the rocket belt was going to stop working after 21 seconds,
sentences.zh: 21秒飞行的关键在于，火箭腰带在21秒后就会停止工作，

sentences.en: even if the pilot was still in the air.
sentences.zh: 即使飞行员当时还在空中。

sentences.en: To make sure the rocket belt pilots didn't wipe out midair,
sentences.zh: 为了确保火箭腰带飞行员不会在空中坠毁，

sentences.en: Bell developed a special helmet with a built-in warning system.
sentences.zh: 贝尔开发了一种带有内置警告系统的特殊头盔。

sentences.en: It was a vibrator that fit against the back of your skull.
sentences.zh: 那是一个贴在你头骨后方的振动器。

sentences.en: Because they tried lights and everything as a warning system.
sentences.zh: 因为他们尝试过灯光等各种东西作为警告系统。

sentences.en: And the mental overload, they ended up with the vibrator on the skull.
sentences.zh: 由于精神超负荷，他们最终采用了贴在头骨上的振动器。

sentences.en: So at 10 seconds, you get a buzz.
sentences.zh: 所以在10秒时，你会感觉到一次嗡嗡声。

sentences.en: And then you get one every second for five seconds.
sentences.zh: 然后接下来的五秒里，每秒都会震动一次。

sentences.en: So get your affairs in order.
sentences.zh: 所以把你的后事安排好吧。

sentences.en: Granted, the helmet didn't solve all possible safety probleMs.
sentences.zh: 当然，这款头盔并没有解决所有可能存在的安全问题。

sentences.en: Bill Suter remembers his first bad test on the rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 比尔·苏特还记得他在火箭腰带上的第一次糟糕测试。

sentences.en: The flight plan was to go straight up 20, 25 feet inside the hangar.
sentences.zh: 飞行计划是在机库内笔直向上飞20、25英尺。

sentences.en: And then move forward and stop, turn around, come back, and land.
sentences.zh: 然后向前移动并停下，转身，返回，然后着陆。

sentences.en: Rose up when I'm about 25 feet up.
sentences.zh: 当我升到大约25英尺高时。

sentences.en: I put it into, you know, a hover position.
sentences.zh: 我让它进入了，你知道的，悬停状态。

sentences.en: And the throttle handle came off in my hand.
sentences.zh: 结果油门手柄脱落在我手里。

sentences.en: Thanks to the safety tether, everything turned out okay and Bill wasn't hurt.
sentences.zh: 多亏了安全系绳，一切结果都还好，比尔没有受伤。

sentences.en: But this is the kind of accident that would turn off certain people, people like me, from the idea of a rocket belt.
sentences.zh: 但这正是那种会让某些人，像我这样的人，对火箭腰带望而却步的事故。

sentences.en: He says he got the hang of it quickly.
sentences.zh: 他说他很快就掌握了窍门。

sentences.en: And the controls, they felt like ice skating.
sentences.zh: 那些操纵杆，感觉就像溜冰一样。

sentences.en: He developed this rhythm with the belt that he called body English.
sentences.zh: 他与腰带培养出了一种他称之为身体语言的节奏。

sentences.en: After his training was complete, Bell Aerospace decided Bill Suter was ready to show the world what the rocket belt was capable of.
sentences.zh: 训练结束后，贝尔航空航天公司认为比尔·苏特已经准备好向世界展示火箭腰带的能力了。

sentences.en: So he packed his bags and shipped out to glamorous Sacramento, California.
sentences.zh: 于是他收拾行囊，出发前往迷人的加利福尼亚州萨克拉门托。

sentences.en: Miss Teenage USA or something like that to do with some national contest every year.
sentences.zh: 美国全美青少年小姐或者每年与某种全国比赛相关的活动。

sentences.en: I wanted to know if Bell could bring the rocket belt to display it here at the Teenage Fair or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 我想知道贝尔能否把火箭腰带带到这里，在青少年博览会或无论什么活动上展示。

sentences.en: It's the first time I'd ever seen the ocean or, you know, I'd never been out of Youngstown.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次见到大海，或者说，我从未离开过扬斯敦。

sentences.en: Bill Suter had never been on an airplane before.
sentences.zh: 比尔·苏特以前从未坐过飞机。

sentences.en: He'd never even stayed in a hotel.
And he certainly hadn't flown a rocket belt over a crowd of thousands of cheering spectators under a spotlight at night.
sentences.zh: 他当然也没有在夜晚的聚光灯下，在数千名欢呼观众的人群头顶上驾驶过火箭腰带。

sentences.en: Well, the light from the outside fairgrounds made it like twilight.
sentences.zh: 嗯，外面集市的灯光让那里看起来像黄昏一样。

sentences.en: Well, it was darker than twilight.
But then they wanted all the lights in the racetrack.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们想要赛马场里的所有灯光都亮起来。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be a surprise.
That's a fart with a lump in it.
sentences.zh: 这简直是个糟透了的烂主意。

sentences.en: And there's brilliant, bright, big spotlights right on me.
sentences.zh: 耀眼、明亮的大型聚光灯直接照在我身上。

sentences.en: I said, that light's blinding me.
sentences.zh: 我说，那光快把我闪瞎了。

sentences.en: I got to get that out of my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我得把那光从眼前移开。

sentences.en: Just before the flight, the lights went down.
sentences.zh: 就在飞行前夕，灯光暗了下来。

sentences.en: For this trick to work, Bill had to fly just over the crowd, close enough they could see him and the rocket belt,
sentences.zh: 为了让这个把戏成功，比尔必须从人群上方飞过，近到他们能看清他和火箭腰带，

sentences.en: and then make a very careful landing on a narrow stage.
sentences.zh: 然后在一个狭窄的舞台上非常小心地着陆。

sentences.en: So on cue, I take off and I'm to fly down the racetrack.
sentences.zh: 于是在暗示下，我起飞了，准备沿赛马场飞下去。
